messages:
support_riley: FYI customer (AcmePayments) hit a big burst this morning and now seeing a mix of 429s and very high per-request latency. They say it started around 08:10 UTC after a retry storm from their side.
support_riley: Logs from customer show a bunch of `429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and then slow 200s that take 2-3s each. They think the KV cache is starving and batching is delaying responses.
customer_ops: attaching their minimal repro: they fire 50 concurrent reqs with small prompts, then retry any failures quickly. They used the hosted /v1/generate endpoint.
customer_ops: repro curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}' \
  --parallel 50 --retry 0
```
support_riley: Important notes: they are not using streaming, and they pinned model to `rwd-13b` (hosted). They reported this persists even after backoff.
jordan_oncall: thanks, digging in. Two hypotheses: (1) API quota/rate limiter hit (global token or per-tenant token bucket) causing 429s; (2) continuous batching + KV cache warmup causing perceived throttling — when many concurrent small requests, batching may wait to fill, causing latency; then KV cache misses add CPU/GPU overhead.
jordan_oncall: can you share the raw request ids or a sample request_id? that helps map to gateway logs.
support_riley: gave sample request_id: req_0a1b2c3d4e. Also seeing a pattern: 429s cluster for ~30s then long tail of 200s.
maria_mlinfra: I pulled the gateway trace for req_0a1b2c3d4e. Gateway returned 429 upstream due to the tenant token bucket hitting burst capacity. After that, we routed some traffic to fallback smaller model for a bit. KV cache hit rate dropped to ~20% during the spike.
maria_mlinfra: quick note on behavior: when quota is exhausted we gate requests at the proxy layer — that can free resources but cause retries and bursts when clients backoff incorrectly. The low KV hit rate explains extra latency on subsequent successful requests.
maria_mlinfra: reproduced locally with a small harness: firing 60 parallel short requests against a single serving instance with continuous batching enabled leads to batch creation delay ~70-120ms and KV misses on many requests causing 200s latency bump.
jordan_oncall: repro steps (internal):
```
# spawn 60 concurrent single-token requests against local runtime
python stress.py --concurrency 60 --prompt 'hi' --model rwd-13b --no-stream
# observe batch windows and kv miss metrics in /metrics
```
support_riley: Customer is asking for mitigations — they'd prefer to avoid 429s during short spikes. What's recommended?
maria_mlinfra: immediate options: (1) increase tenant burst quota (if account allows) to absorb their short storms; (2) recommend client-side jittered exponential backoff and convex retry to avoid retry storms; (3) enable streaming/partial responses if they can; (4) for Hosted we can pin them to a flavor with higher concurrency or route to Dedicated if sustained. Also we can temporarily increase KV cache warmup TTL to reduce misses.
jordan_oncall: ops action: temporarily bumped their burst quota by +2x for 15 minutes to see if it helps. Also enabled a warmup prefetch on a subset of hosts serving that tenant to try to raise KV hit rate.
support_riley: customer confirmed lower 429s after an hour but still some perceived slow tail on success responses. They notice that immediate retries after a 429 often succeed but are slower.
maria_mlinfra: that matches the batching/caching interaction: when the KV cache is cold, the runtime must load embeddings/KV pages which increases per-token time; batching can reduce throughput for tiny requests if batch windows wait. Both combine to make retries feel slower post-429.
billing_ana: flagged in case customer thinks it's billing-related. No pattern to billing spikes in their invoice.
jordan_oncall: longer term fixes: (a) adopt adaptive batch windows — shrink batch wait thresholds under high concurrency/short-request regimes; (b) smarter KV prefetch heuristics keyed by prefix/tenant; (c) more transparent 429 headers indicating cooldown and remaining burst quota so clients can backoff better.
maria_mlinfra: TODOs: 1) run a controlled load test reproducer and capture KV hit/miss, batch size distribution, and gateway token bucket fill. 2) add a short-term heuristic to favor smaller batches for sub-100-token requests. 3) build a dashboard for perceived-throttle events per tenant.
support_riley: I've summarized and shared with AcmePayments ops. They want an SLA note for mitigation and ask if we can provide client-side recommended retry policy text.
ordan_placeholder: @support_riley (accidentally typed), here's a suggested snippet for clients: exponential backoff with full jitter, cap retries to 3, randomize initial delay between 50-150ms, and on 429 prefer an added jittered delay of 200-500ms before retry.
support_riley: thanks — will send that. Closing loop: customer asks if there's anything they should change now. Recommendation: add jittered backoff + reduce retry concurrency spikes; we will follow up on infra short-term changes. :thumbsup:
